symmGroup.statement: For a measurable random variable $X:\Omega\to G$, defines the symmetry group $\mathrm{Sym}[X]$: the additive subgroup of $G$ consisting of all $h\in G$ such that $X+h$ has the same distribution as $X$.

sub_mem_symmGroup.statement: Let $X$ be a measurable $G$-valued random variable with $d[X;X]=0$, and let $x,y\in G$ satisfy $P[X=x]\neq 0$ and $P[X=y]\neq 0$. Then $x-y\in\mathrm{Sym}[X]$.
sub_mem_symmGroup.sketch: Taking an independent copy and using that the Ruzsa distance vanishes, one obtains an entropy identity which, via $I[X:Y]=H[X]-H[X|Y]$ and the characterization $I[X:Y]=0\iff X,Y$ independent, yields an independence statement; then the conditional entropy is invariant under injective shifts ($H[f(Y,X)|Y]=H[X|Y]$), and independence gives $H[X|Y]=H[X]$, from which one deduces that $X$ and $X+(x-y)$ are identically distributed.

isUniform_sub_const_of_rdist_eq_zero.statement: Let $X$ be a measurable $G$-valued random variable with $d[X;X]=0$, and let $x_0\in G$ satisfy $P[X=x_0]\neq 0$. Then $X-x_0$ is uniformly distributed on the subgroup $\mathrm{Sym}[X]$.
isUniform_sub_const_of_rdist_eq_zero.sketch: By the previous result, any two values $x,y$ of positive probability satisfy $x-y\in\mathrm{Sym}[X]$; combining this with the definition of membership in $\mathrm{Sym}[X]$ shows that $X-x_0$ is supported on $\mathrm{Sym}[X]$ and has equal mass on each of its elements.

exists_isUniform_of_rdist_self_eq_zero.statement: Let $X$ be a measurable $G$-valued random variable with $d[X;X]=0$. Then there exist a subgroup $H\le G$ and a measurable random variable $U$, uniformly distributed on $H$, such that $d[X;U]=0$.
exists_isUniform_of_rdist_self_eq_zero.sketch: Pick $x_0$ with $P[X=x_0]>0$ (possible since $X$ has finite range) and take $H=\mathrm{Sym}[X]$ and $U=X-x_0$, which is uniform on $H$ by the previous result; then $d[X;U]=d[X;X]=0$ because Ruzsa distance is invariant under adding a constant.

exists_isUniform_of_rdist_eq_zero.statement: Let $X$ and $X'$ be measurable $G$-valued random variables with $d[X;X']=0$. Then there exist a subgroup $H\le G$ and a measurable random variable $U$, uniformly distributed on $H$, such that $d[X;U]=0$ and $d[X';U]=0$.
exists_isUniform_of_rdist_eq_zero.sketch: By the triangle inequality $d[X;X]\le d[X;X']+d[X';X]=0$, so the previous result gives $H$ and $U$ with $d[X;U]=0$; then $d[X';U]\le d[X';X]+d[X;U]=0$ by the triangle inequality again (with nonnegativity of Ruzsa distance and the entropy bound $|H[X]-H[Y]|\le 2d[X;Y]$ used along the way).
